The lab is tier T2: real Python and R executing inside the browser through
WebAssembly. Nothing is sent to a server, because there is no server — the
whole site is static files.

The point of this tier is not speed but **agency**. A chapter can assert that
a naive difference is biased; a lab cell lets you change the numbers and watch
it happen. Every cell is editable and re-runnable.

The cost is an engine boot of roughly 5–15 seconds the first time a page needs
Python or R. After that, execution is fast.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What runs here and what does not

Available in the browser: `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `statsmodels`,
`matplotlib`, `plotly`, `scikit-learn`, and a wasm-built subset of CRAN.

Not available: `econml`, `dowhy`, and anything else relying on compiled
extensions. Those live in the chapters' build-time charts, where a real
interpreter does the work.
:::
